newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan PDVSA says oil strike turnout partial.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan PDVSA says oil strike turnout partial.

text.p: Venezuelan state oil company PDVSA said Friday that an eight-hour strike by workers attracted only partial adherence and that operations were being maintained as normal by non-union staff.
The strike by unions Fedepetrol and Fetrahidrocarburos to protest salary levels began at 0500 local time Friday.
"The strike call has been obeyed partially and operations are being maintained by professional staff, in line with the contingency plan," said PDVSA spokesmwoman Esther Bermudez.

Earlier, a spokesman at the 305,000 barrel per day (bpd) Cardon refinery said there was only 11 percent adherence to the strike call by union members there. He added that product exports were proceeding as normal and that the refinery was running at capacity.
However, Fedepetrol union president Carlos Ortega told Reuters on Friday morning that preliminary indications from the regions showed that the strike was a "total success".
PDVSA's Bermudez said the average PDVSA worker's monthly wage was 150,000-180,000 Bolivars ($315-380).
